sources.researchNote: The advertisement itself carries no date. The Gallica notice for ark:/12148/bpt6k6579174s identifies the digitised object as Le Sport universel illustré of 15 October 1935, and leaf 3 of that issue carries the advertisement; the date recorded here comes from that notice. The printing is about a year later than the Paris stay the image illustrates.

media.title: Paris Years — document gallery
media.description: Document gallery for Kaper’s Paris years, 1933–1934. It brings together French and European press documentation, materials relating to French film work, two distinct photographs from the November 1933 reception for Jan Kiepura, and a Paris hotel context image.
media.altText: Gallery card for Bronisław Kaper’s Paris years, combining press items, posters and contextual materials.
media.publicCaption: Gallery of press items, posters and contextual materials relating to Bronisław Kaper’s Paris years and his work in French cinema and theatrical culture, 1933–1934.
media.rightsNote: This gallery has no single rights status. Each member medium carries its own public-domain, licensed, restricted or unresolved-copyright statement; reuse must be assessed item by item.
media.publicCreditLine: Item-level credits identify the holding institution and source for every gallery member.

media.title: Hôtel Le Château Frontenac, 54 rue Pierre Charron, Paris — advertisement, 1935
media.description: Advertisement for the Hôtel Le Château Frontenac, 54 rue Pierre Charron, Paris 8e, printed in Le Sport universel illustré on 15 October 1935. It shows the building about a year after Kaper left for the United States, and is used here as a context image of the address rather than as a document of his stay.
media.altText: Black-and-white advertisement showing the exterior of Hôtel Le Château Frontenac at 54 rue Pierre Charron in Paris, with room prices in francs.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The advertisement reproduces a photograph of the hotel and was printed in Le Sport universel illustré on 15 October 1935 without a photographer’s or designer’s credit, so it is treated as an anonymous work, for which the French term of seventy years from publication ran out at the end of 2005. It was accordingly still protected in France on 1 January 1996 and the URAA restored United States copyright for ninety-five years from publication, to the end of 2030. Gallica supplies the digitised page under conditions governed by French law, which exclude documents protected by a third party’s copyright and leave reuse in another country to the user. Source gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France.
